terms.prefLabel: Build and publish the site from the AST
terms.definition: The site route's steps, provided by the mounted layers and run by `stage-local.ts` → `build-instance-site.ts`: the landing layer's IG API sidecars when it has the step (`ig-site:sidecars`), the artefact index from the AST and the thin pages with the IG composed at the root (`ig-site:compose`: `ast-to-artifact-index.ts`, `gen-ig-pages.ts --compiled-data ast-data`), the OpenAPI pages when the IG holds them (`ig-site:openapi`), the AST's resources served as `ast-data/` and the build stamp (`ig-site:publisher-pages`). Published at the root from the default branch, as a preview otherwise.

Actions → "IG AST refresh (by hand)" → Run workflow on the default branch, inputs `ref` = the default branch, `force` = false. The publish refused, so the verdict already says the cache is not valid; `force` is for a cache that is valid but suspected wrong.

terms.prefLabel: Build the IG with the AST exporter
terms.definition: The runner mounts the layers the IG repository's `index.lock.json` pins, restores and judges the cache itself, and, when it is not valid, runs the caller's optional `pre-export` overlay command, then `AstExportCli` (Tool `ig-ast-export`, `litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher` at the pinned `claude/ast-export` commit) with `-tx`. The inputs `pre-export` changed are put back and the AST is recorded against the clean commit's input digest (`ig-ast.ts source-inputs`). The AST just built must itself be `valid` for the commit, or the run fails.

terms.prefLabel: Restore and judge the cached AST
terms.definition: `ig-cache.sh restore --ig-root .` fetches `cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>` into `output-ast/` (with the Publisher's `txcache/`), then `ig-cache.sh verify` runs `ig-ast.ts validity`: exit 0 valid, 1 stale-inputs (naming which input), 2 cannot-tell. A restore that finds no branch is a miss, judged as not valid. In an IG repository's site route this is the first `pre` step, `ig-site:ast` (`ig-repo-site.ts ast`).

`ig-cache.sh seed --ig-root . --push`: one commit holding the AST, the Publisher's expansions and `txcache/`, its subject recording the package, counts, Publisher version and source commit. Refused when the candidate is under 90% of the incumbent's resources or edges (the no-shrink gate).

`ig-ast.ts diff <base> <head> --plan plan.json --site <site>/ast-delta/`: resources added, removed, changed (with an element-level differential) and version-changed; edges added and removed; the plan's decision. Every page opens with the provisional mark and is wrapped in raw so narrative Liquid is not executed.

terms.prefLabel: Note the missed coupling on the bean
terms.definition: Append to bean `a9tx` (W8): the resource key, the differential path, and why it is unexplained. Check before creating: beans create is not idempotent. A note, not a new bean, unless the owner asks for one.

Start at the delta index; open each changed resource's page. Check `builtAt` before judging: a resource carried from the base was not rebuilt, so a difference there is the change itself or a missed coupling, never noise. The differential is structural: a reordered repeating element shows at every index.

terms.prefLabel: Check the base AST against the inputs
terms.definition: `ig-ast.ts validity <base> --ig <root>`: folio-assistant-core's compiledValidity on the manifest's inputs, with the input digest recomputed by the same algorithm as the Java writer. Exit 0 valid, 1 stale-inputs (names which input), 2 cannot-tell. Run against the BASE revision's checkout.

terms.prefLabel: Restricted checkout of the backward cone
terms.definition: git sparse-checkout of the cone's files plus sushi-config.yaml, ig.ini and the alias files — a median of three files, p90 eleven, measured on the SMART Immunizations IG.

terms.prefLabel: Compute the cone of the change
terms.definition: content/pipeline/fsh-cone.ts over the changed files: the forward cone is what to rebuild, the backward cone is what to check out.

terms.prefLabel: Post the cone report on the PR
terms.definition: Review path: the reviewer sees what this change rebuilds — how many artefacts, and whether a hub (a shared RuleSet, CQL library or value set) is touched — before the build finishes. On main it is a log line.

terms.prefLabel: Load or reuse the warm context
terms.definition: The validator's server mode holds the loaded dependency packages, snapshots and expansions in its session cache. Cold start loads the restored derived FHIR rather than regenerating it.

Deploy the site built from main or a release. Deploying is release-management, after a human authorised the release — an agent never records that authorisation. Report the published URL only once it answers: a returned deploy is not a serving site.
A preview never seeds the shared cache.
Exit 1 or 3 from restore: the whole IG is built as today. Its outputs become the records the next seed writes.
The whole-IG aggregates only — artifacts, TOC, canonicals, expansions, package, QA aggregate. Never re-derives an artefact: a missing record is a miss (exit 1), not a silent rebuild.

terms.prefLabel: Log the environment error on the bean
terms.definition: Exit 2 from restore: the cache store or the toolchain could not be reached. Record that on the change's bean, with the restore output, so the work plan says the build did not run and why. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent.
Validation failed: record the findings on the change's bean, so the work plan says what blocks it. Check before creating — beans create is not idempotent.
Combine the restored per-artefact records with the cone's freshly rendered ones into one complete set, so the meta-index rebuild that follows has every artefact's record and never re-derives one.

terms.prefLabel: Run QC gates on the aggregate QA
terms.definition: qa.json is the aggregate of per-artefact outcomes; the reviewer reads the cone's rows first.
QC failed on the aggregate: file each finding as a bean, so it is tracked on the work plan rather than lost in qa.json. Check for an existing bean before creating one.

terms.prefLabel: Re-render the cone's records (fhir_narrative · skip lists)
terms.definition: Narrative and fragments for the cone only: the publisher's -no-validate / -no-narrative complements today, Rapido's differential build once its tracker is persisted.
ig-cache restore: per-artefact records, the terminology cache, the package cache and temp/, keyed by the toolchain slug. Exit 0 usable, 1 miss, 2 environment error, 3 present but toolchain moved.

terms.prefLabel: Seed the cache from the green build
terms.definition: Only a green build of main or a release seeds. Seed writes to the -test branch, verifies a restore from a clean clone, then promotes.
Assemble the site from the merged records: the IG template and a Jekyll build over output/. Only site assembly happens here — every artefact record already exists.

Compile the restricted checkout with SUSHI — the cone's FSH, not the whole IG. A build optimisation, not a validation shortcut: SUSHI compiling is not conformance, so a green compile goes on to validation rather than standing in for it.

Validate the cone's resources against the warm validator and report the cone that was checked. A validator that could not start is could-not-determine, never a pass with no findings. A green cone is not a green IG: a profile the change did not touch can still be broken by it.

Write the FSH profiles, value sets and definitions the source model calls for. This is the stage where profiles, slicing and invariants belong — a decision that can only be expressed in FHIR comes here, not back into the source model.

Run the IG Publisher: it renders output/, writes each resource's JSON, the package, canonicals and qa.json, and does the two things no cache can — validates every resource against its profiles and resolves the dependency closure with terminology expansion.
Release authorisation and review follow draft-to-publication.bpmn.
QC findings do not stay in a report nobody re-reads — each becomes a bean the modeller and the agents both see.

The QC reviewer rules on the aggregate QA against the publication gates. Emitting the QA report is mechanical; ruling on it is a decision, which is why it sits in the reviewer's lane rather than the build's.
Compile the FSH to FHIR JSON with SUSHI. Compiling is not conformance: a green SUSHI result goes on to validation and never stands in for it.

Validate the compiled resources against their profiles and the packages they constrain. A validator that could not start is could-not-determine, never a pass with an empty findings list. Failures return to authoring.
cat-harness Process_WireframeDesignReview: as-is use for a form that exists, design use for one being designed. This process does not restate the method.

terms.prefLabel: Apply it to the other side
terms.definition: The side the request edited is the source of the change (owner, 2026-10-14). An edited Questionnaire is applied as an FSH edit and the wireframe is redrawn to match; an edited wireframe is kept and the Questionnaire re-derived from it. Then back to Task_Read.

terms.prefLabel: Ask for review with deep links
terms.definition: One deep link per rendered Questionnaire and wireframe, before and after. Where the request goes — the conversation, an issue, the pull request — is a judgement, and more than one may be right: staging-review's deep-link rule, point 5.

fhir-harness/scripts/check-wireframe-questionnaire.ts <wireframe.html> <Questionnaire.json>, per layout. Exit 0 faithful, 1 a finding, 2 cannot tell, which is never a pass. The findings become the output's fidelity[] and are shown to the reviewers.
fsh-generated/resources/Questionnaire-<id>.json, or the IG's published Questionnaire-<id>.json — never FSH. The JSON is what every renderer and reader receives, so it is what is judged.

terms.prefLabel: Render the wireframe and the LHC-Forms view
terms.definition: A mid-fidelity wireframe with one field per answerable item, each carrying data-element and sitting in a data-layout web or mobile subtree; and the form view, the same JSON in the vendored <lhc-forms> web component on the IG site's form page. Never a CDN at runtime (owner, 2026-10-14).

terms.prefLabel: Review the staged form and wireframe
terms.definition: At the deep links. A change is requested through ✍ suggest in its Questionnaire mode, or the questionnaire-change issue form, and says which side was edited: the Questionnaire or the wireframe.
cat-harness Tool wireframe-check: 1280×800 and 390×844; renders, no-overflow and no-placeholder, each a script entry. A rendering missing either viewport does not enter review.
The branch's wireframes and form pages published under branches/<slug>/ by feature-staging.
